{'index': 0, 'translation': "A new market intelligence report indicates that the memory Apple is paying for the iPhone 18 Pro will cost four times as much as last year's model."}

{'index': 1, 'translation': "TrendForce says Apple won't pass on the full cost to consumers, and will increasingly rely on services revenue to offset the rising cost of hardware production..."}

{'index': 2, 'translation': 'Apple announced significant price hikes for most of its products back in June, noting that it had done everything it could to delay the increases but had no choice.'}

{'index': 3, 'translation': "Apple didn't raise the price of existing iPhones at the time, but that situation is expected to change next week. TrendForce points out a significant increase in memory costs for the new models."}

{'index': 4, 'translation': 'Apple is not expected to pass on the full increase in memory costs to iPhone pricing. Current estimates are that the iPhone 17 Pro will see a price hike of around $100.'}

{'index': 5, 'translation': "The reason is that aggressive price hikes would lead even the most loyal Apple fans to upgrade less frequently. TrendForce says Apple wouldn't want to sacrifice its continued growth momentum, pointing to a weak macroeconomic environment that makes consumers more cautious in their spending."}

{'index': 6, 'translation': "The firm predicts Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Ultra, could start at as much as $2,299, with top configurations exceeding $3,000."}
